Maintenance Report — MNT-0088-002

Asset: WELL-0088 (SW-24 Well 088, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2023 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 17 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0088-0012 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 08 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0088-0012 at 07:15 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.9% of the pad area, estimated 2.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 284 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 227 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

  • About 2.8 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0088-002 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0088-012

Asset: WELL-0088 (SW-24 Well 088, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 25 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 13 Mar 2024 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 419 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0088-0071 on 2024-02-22 Report written: 15 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0088-0071 showed the wellhead at 15.1 °C with the air at 12.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Bearing grease and consumables413

Total3,081

Compliance check

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 1 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0088-031

Asset: WELL-0088 (SW-24 Well 088, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 05 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 14 Jul 2026 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 217 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0088-0193 on 2026-07-02 Report written: 15 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0088-0193 showed the wellhead at 46.6 °C with the air at 37.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 284 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 227 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0088-031 (WS-06).
